claim: Nucleosomes are comprised of approximately 147 bp of DNA surrounding an octamer of core histone proteins H2A, H2B, H3, and H4.
source: Nucleosomes, the fundamental repeating unit of chromatin, are comprised of approximately 147 bp of DNA surrounding an octamer of core histone proteins H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 (Luger et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Luger et al., 1997, which is a well-known structural study of the nucleosome.

claim: The cleavage and polyadenylation (CPA) pathway functions at protein-coding genes in S. cerevisiae.
source: The cleavage and polyadenylation (CPA) pathway, which functions at protein-coding genes, requires the concerted activities of proteins in the CPF, CF1A and CF1B complexes.
evidence: This claim is stated directly in the text as part of the description of termination pathways.

claim: The Nrd1-Nab3-Sen1 (NNS) termination pathway is primarily dedicated to the termination of short noncoding transcripts in yeast.
source: The Nrd1-Nab3-Sen1 (NNS) termination pathway is primarily dedicated to the termination of short noncoding transcripts in yeast, including small nuclear RNAs (snRNAs), small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs), cryptic unstable transcripts (CUTs), Nrd1-unterminated transcripts (NUTs) and aborted transcripts from protein-coding genes (Porrua and Libri, 2015; Arndt and Reines, 2015; Schulz et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Nine amino acid substitutions in H3 and one amino acid substitution in H4 cause readthrough of the SNR47 terminator in the reporter.
source: We identified nine amino acid substitutions in H3 and one amino acid substitution in H4 that cause readthrough of the SNR47 terminator in the reporter, as measured by growth on media lacking histidine (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B, which displays growth assays.

claim: Many of the H3 residues altered in the termination-defective mutants localize to the DNA entry-exit site of the nucleosome.
source: Many of the H3 residues altered in the termination-defective mutants localize to the DNA entry-exit site of the nucleosome (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 1E, which displays the nucleosome structure with highlighted residues.

claim: The DNA entry-exit site is composed of the H3 αN helix, the preceding H3 tail region, and the H2A C-terminal tail.
source: The DNA entry-exit site is composed of the H3 αN helix, the preceding H3 tail region, and the H2A C-terminal tail (Luger et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the Luger et al., 1997 structural study.

claim: 30/73 (41.1%) of Pol II-transcribed snoRNAs are read through at least 1.5-fold more than wild type in the H3 T45A mutant.
source: By this metric, 30/73 (41.1%) and 43/73 (58.9%) of Pol II-transcribed snoRNAs are read through at least 1.5-fold more than wild type in the H3 T45A mutant and H3 R52A mutant, respectively (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 2A-B.

claim: 43/73 (58.9%) of Pol II-transcribed snoRNAs are read through at least 1.5-fold more than wild type in the H3 R52A mutant.
source: By this metric, 30/73 (41.1%) and 43/73 (58.9%) of Pol II-transcribed snoRNAs are read through at least 1.5-fold more than wild type in the H3 T45A mutant and H3 R52A mutant, respectively (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 2A-B.

claim: Levels of NUTs increase by 2.19-fold in the H3 T45A mutant relative to wild type.
source: As measured by RNA-seq, levels of NUTs increase by 2.19-fold in the H3 T45A mutant and 2.57-fold in the H3 R52A mutant relative to wild type, arguing that the NNS defect in these histone mutant strains is not specific to SNR gene termination (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: Levels of NUTs increase by 2.57-fold in the H3 R52A mutant relative to wild type.
source: As measured by RNA-seq, levels of NUTs increase by 2.19-fold in the H3 T45A mutant and 2.57-fold in the H3 R52A mutant relative to wild type, arguing that the NNS defect in these histone mutant strains is not specific to SNR gene termination (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: The increase in sense-strand RNA levels in the H3 T45A and H3 R52A mutants in the region 150 bp downstream of the CPS is modest but statistically significant.
source: For the region 150 bp downstream of the CPS, the increase in sense-strand RNA levels in the H3 T45A and H3 R52A mutants is modest but statistically significant (Figure 3B; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: H3 K36me3 levels are greatly reduced in the H3 R49A and H3 R52A mutant strains.
source: In agreement with published results (Du and Briggs, 2010; Endo et al., 2012), H3 K36me3 levels are greatly reduced in the H3 R49A and H3 R52A mutant strains, while other DNA entry-exit site mutants, including the H3 T45A mutant, exhibit a modest decrease in the H3 K36me3 signal (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5A and citations to published results.

claim: Both DNA entry-exit site mutants showed upregulation of SRAT expression by greater than four-fold relative to a wild-type control strain.
source: Both DNA entry-exit site mutants showed upregulation of SRAT expression by greater than four-fold relative to a wild-type control strain (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: An H3 R52A set2∆ double mutant exhibits a strong synthetic growth defect.
source: Instead, our results indicate a strong synthetic growth defect in the H3 R52A set2∆ double mutant (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by plasmid shuffle assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The H3 K36A, R52A double mutant is inviable.
source: Unlike the H3 K36A and H3 R52A single mutants, the H3 K36A, R52A double mutant is inviable (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by plasmid shuffle assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Single-residue alanine substitutions in the DNA entry-exit site do not alter levels of H3 K56ac.
source: Unlike H3 K36me3, our data show that single-residue alanine substitutions in the DNA entry-exit site do not alter levels of H3 K56ac (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), suggesting that the transcription defects caused by these substitutions are not due to a general loss of this multifunctional histone modification.
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: H3 R52A nucleosomes appear more sensitive to MNase than wild-type nucleosomes.
source: Based on this assessment, H3 R52A nucleosomes appear more sensitive to MNase than wild-type nucleosomes, as evidenced by reduced levels of di-, tri-, and higher order nucleosomes at comparable treatments (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by MNase digestion data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Nucleosome occupancy in the H3 R52A mutant is reduced both within coding regions and flanking intergenic regions relative to the wild-type control strain.
source: Relative to the wild-type control strain, nucleosome occupancy in the H3 R52A mutant is reduced both within coding regions and flanking intergenic regions (Figure 6A–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by MNase-seq data shown in Figure 6A–D.

claim: In the region 150 bp downstream of the CPS, there is a statistically significant reduction in nucleosome occupancy in the H3 R52A mutant.
source: In the region 150 bp downstream of the CPS, we observed a statistically significant reduction in nucleosome occupancy (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by MNase-seq data analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The superbinder sequence increases nucleosome occupancy approximately 3-fold in wild-type cells.
source: These data show that the superbinder sequence increases nucleosome occupancy approximately 3-fold in wild-type cells and 2.5-fold in H3 R52A mutant cells (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The superbinder sequence increases nucleosome occupancy approximately 2.5-fold in H3 R52A mutant cells.
source: These data show that the superbinder sequence increases nucleosome occupancy approximately 3-fold in wild-type cells and 2.5-fold in H3 R52A mutant cells (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The increase in nucleosome occupancy downstream of SNR48 imparted by the superbinder sequence suppresses the termination defect of the H3 R52A mutant to the level of a wild-type strain lacking the superbinder.
source: Interestingly, the increase in nucleosome occupancy downstream of SNR48 imparted by the superbinder sequence suppresses the termination defect of the H3 R52A mutant to the level of a wild-type strain lacking the superbinder (Figure 7D).
evidence: This claim is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The superbinder sequence is sufficient to suppress basal level transcription readthrough observed in the wild-type strain.
source: The superbinder sequence is also sufficient to suppress basal level transcription readthrough observed in the wild-type strain.
evidence: This claim is stated directly in the text and is supported by the northern blot data in Figure 7D.

claim: Unterminated polymerases can continue transcribing into neighboring genes and interfere with their expression.
source: Unterminated polymerases can continue transcribing into neighboring genes and interfere with their expression (Greger and Proudfoot, 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Greger and Proudfoot, 1998.

claim: Widespread transcription termination defects can result from cell stress or viral infection.
source: Widespread transcription termination defects can result from cell stress (Vilborg et al., 2015) or viral infection (Nemeroff et al., 1998; Rutkowski et al., 2015) and are observed in numerous human cancers (Grosso et al., 2015; Kannan et al., 2011; Maher et al., 2009; Varley et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Widespread transcription termination defects are observed in numerous human cancers.
source: Widespread transcription termination defects can result from cell stress (Vilborg et al., 2015) or viral infection (Nemeroff et al., 1998; Rutkowski et al., 2015) and are observed in numerous human cancers (Grosso et al., 2015; Kannan et al., 2011; Maher et al., 2009; Varley et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Defects in Paf1C and its dependent histone modifications cause terminator readthrough of NNS-dependent snoRNA genes.
source: Defects in Paf1C and its dependent histone modifications cause terminator readthrough of NNS-dependent snoRNA genes (Ellison et al., 2019; Terzi et al., 2011; Tomson et al., 2013; Tomson et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Loss of Paf1C subunits leads to changes in polyA site selection at specific protein-coding genes in yeast.
source: In addition, loss of Paf1C subunits leads to changes in polyA site selection at specific protein-coding genes in yeast (Penheiter et al., 2005), a phenomenon also observed in mammalian cells (Yang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Penheiter et al., 2005 and Yang et al., 2016.

claim: ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers Isw1 and Chd1 have been linked to transcription termination of some mRNAs.
source: ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers Isw1 and Chd1, which regulate nucleosome spacing within gene bodies and near the CPS, have been linked to transcription termination of some mRNAs (Alén et al., 2002; Morillon et al., 2003; Ocampo et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Chromatin-associated general regulatory factors (GRFs), such as Reb1, function as roadblocks to the progression of Pol II.
source: These studies identified chromatin-associated general regulatory factors (GRFs), such as Reb1, as roadblocks to the progression of Pol II working as either part of the NNS-dependent termination pathway (Roy et al., 2016) or as an independent termination process important for blocking readthrough transcription from upstream CPA and NNS terminators (Candelli et al., 2018; Colin et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Roy et al., 2016, Candelli et al., 2018, and Colin et al., 2014.

claim: Amino acid substitutions at the DNA entry-exit site increase the intrinsic mobility of nucleosomes and DNA unwrapping around the histone octamer in vitro.
source: Amino acid substitutions at the DNA entry-exit site, including H3 R52A and T45A, increase the intrinsic mobility of nucleosomes and DNA unwrapping around the histone octamer in vitro (Ferreira et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ferreira et al., 2007.

claim: Nucleosomes impose structural and kinetic barriers to RNA polymerase II progression.
source: Further, nucleosomes impose structural and kinetic barriers to RNA polymerase II progression (Bondarenko et al., 2006; Farnung et al., 2018; Kujirai et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: H3 K36 methylation by Set2 prevents cryptic initiation from intragenic promoters and antisense transcription across gene bodies.
source: H3 K36 methylation by Set2 prevents cryptic initiation from intragenic promoters and antisense transcription across gene bodies (Carrozza et al., 2005; Joshi and Struhl, 2005; Keogh et al., 2005; Venkatesh et al., 2012; Kim et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: H3 T45 has been shown to be phosphorylated in yeast and mammalian cells with regulatory effects on diverse processes including DNA replication, HP1-mediated transcriptional repression and apoptosis.
source: H3 T45 has been shown to be phosphorylated in yeast and mammalian cells with regulatory effects on diverse processes including DNA replication, HP1-mediated transcriptional repression and apoptosis (Baker et al., 2010; Hurd et al., 2009; Jang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: One study reported elevated H3 T45 phosphorylation downstream of DNA damage response genes by a kinase activated by DNA damage conditions and defective transcription termination at these genes in a mammalian cell line overexpressing H3 T45A.
source: Interestingly, one study reported elevated H3 T45 phosphorylation downstream of DNA damage response genes by a kinase activated by DNA damage conditions and defective transcription termination at these genes in a mammalian cell line overexpressing H3 T45A (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claim: The H3 T45A and H3 R52A mutants exhibit increased antisense transcription over genes.
source: In addition to changes in sense-strand transcription, we also observed that the H3 T45A and H3 R52A substitutions cause increased antisense transcription over genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Decreased Pol II occupancy in the H3 R52A mutant might reflect an increase in Pol II elongation rate as a consequence of disrupted nucleosome structure.
source: While other explanations are possible, decreased Pol II occupancy might reflect an increase in Pol II elongation rate as a consequence of disrupted nucleosome structure in the mutants (Ehrensberger et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is speculative, as indicated by the phrase 'might reflect', and is supported by a citation to Ehrensberger et al., 2013.

claim: The differences in the RNA-seq and 4tU-seq profiles suggest increased stabilization of transcripts at steady state in the histone mutant strains.
source: The differences in the RNA-seq and 4tU-seq profiles further suggest increased stabilization of transcripts at steady state in the histone mutant strains.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of RNA-seq and 4tU-seq data.

claim: Global reductions in RNA synthesis are buffered by mechanisms that increase RNA stability.
source: This observation is in accordance with evidence showing that global reductions in RNA synthesis are buffered by mechanisms that increase RNA stability (Timmers and Tora, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Timmers and Tora, 2018.

claim: Divergently oriented genes show a greater relative enrichment of nascent transcription 5' to the coding region.
source: When viewed as a whole, divergently oriented genes show a greater relative enrichment of nascent transcription 5' to the coding region and convergently oriented genes show a greater relative enrichment of nascent transcription 3' to the coding region (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by 4tU-seq data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Convergently oriented genes show a greater relative enrichment of nascent transcription 3' to the coding region.
source: When viewed as a whole, divergently oriented genes show a greater relative enrichment of nascent transcription 5' to the coding region and convergently oriented genes show a greater relative enrichment of nascent transcription 3' to the coding region (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by 4tU-seq data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The DNA entry-exit site mutants exhibit a range of phenotypes associated with altered chromatin structure and transcription.
source: In summary, these growth assays show that DNA entry-exit site mutants exhibit a range of phenotypes associated with altered chromatin structure and transcription.
evidence: This claim is supported by the growth assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The DNA entry-exit site substitutions affect transcription differently from previously published Sin- mutants, such as H3 V117A.
source: However, in contrast to the Spt-, Bur- and cryptic initiation phenotypes, the DNA entry-exit site mutants did not exhibit the SWI/SNF Independent (Sin-) phenotype, which measures the ability of histone mutants to overcome the absence of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex (Hainer and Martens, 2011; Kruger et al., 1995). This observation suggests that the DNA entry-exit site substitutions affect transcription differently from previously published Sin- mutants, such as H3 V117A (Hainer and Martens, 2011).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that DNA entry-exit site mutants do not exhibit the Sin- phenotype, unlike H3 V117A.

claim: Nucleosome positioning is altered in the H3 R52A mutant with nucleosome peaks shifting downstream of the TSS and widening.
source: In addition to occupancy changes, nucleosome positioning is altered in the mutant with nucleosome peaks shifting downstream of the TSS and widening (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by MNase-seq data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: A region of reduced nucleosome occupancy over the CPS in the H3 R52A mutant correlates with a region of reduced Pol II occupancy.
source: A region of reduced nucleosome occupancy over the CPS in the mutant correlates with a region of reduced Pol II occupancy (Figure 6A,B,D,E), suggesting that the H3 R52A substitution disrupts nucleosomes which may normally slow Pol II transit in the termination region.
evidence: This claim is supported by MNase-seq and ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6A,B,D,E.

claim: The H3 R52A substitution disrupts nucleosomes which may normally slow Pol II transit in the termination region.
source: A region of reduced nucleosome occupancy over the CPS in the mutant correlates with a region of reduced Pol II occupancy (Figure 6A,B,D,E), suggesting that the H3 R52A substitution disrupts nucleosomes which may normally slow Pol II transit in the termination region.
evidence: This claim is speculative, as indicated by the phrase 'suggesting' and 'may normally', and is inferred from the correlation between reduced nucleosome occupancy and reduced Pol II occupancy.

claim: The degree of nucleosome loss in the H3 R52A mutant does not appear to be directly correlated with RNA levels at all genes.
source: However, the degree of nucleosome loss in the mutant does not appear to be directly correlated with RNA levels at all genes, consistent with other factors, such as RNA degradation pathways, contributing to the accumulation of 3'-extended transcripts.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that nucleosome loss and RNA levels are not directly correlated.

claim: Other factors, such as RNA degradation pathways, contribute to the accumulation of 3'-extended transcripts.
source: However, the degree of nucleosome loss in the mutant does not appear to be directly correlated with RNA levels at all genes, consistent with other factors, such as RNA degradation pathways, contributing to the accumulation of 3'-extended transcripts.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that nucleosome loss and RNA levels are not directly correlated.

claim: The reduction in H3 K36me3 in the H3 T45A and H3 R52A mutants likely contributes to the increased antisense transcription.
source: While the reduction in H3 K36me3 likely contributes to the increased antisense transcription in the H3 T45A and H3 R52A mutants (Venkatesh et al., 2016) as well as their SNR gene termination defects (Tomson et al., 2013), we note that these mutants differ significantly in the global levels of this mark and that H3 K36A was not identified as a strong candidate in our termination screen.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the known role of H3 K36me3 in suppressing antisense transcription, supported by citations.

claim: The DNA entry-exit site contributes to transcription fidelity through a mechanism distinct from and in addition to promoting H3 K36 methylation.
source: These observations suggest that the DNA entry-exit site contributes to transcription fidelity through a mechanism distinct from and in addition to promoting H3 K36 methylation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that H3 T45A and H3 R52A mutants have different levels of H3 K36me3 but similar termination defects, and that H3 K36A was not identified in the screen.

claim: The H3 R52A substitution is synthetically lethal with deletion of SET2.
source: In support of this, we found that the H3 R52A substitution is synthetically lethal with deletion of SET2 or the H3 K36A substitution, indicating that these H3 residues function, at least in part, through separate pathways.
evidence: This claim is supported by the plasmid shuffle assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The H3 R52A substitution is synthetically lethal with the H3 K36A substitution.
source: In support of this, we found that the H3 R52A substitution is synthetically lethal with deletion of SET2 or the H3 K36A substitution, indicating that these H3 residues function, at least in part, through separate pathways.
evidence: This claim is supported by the plasmid shuffle assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: H3 R52A and H3 K36A function, at least in part, through separate pathways.
source: In support of this, we found that the H3 R52A substitution is synthetically lethal with deletion of SET2 or the H3 K36A substitution, indicating that these H3 residues function, at least in part, through separate pathways.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the synthetic lethality observed between H3 R52A and H3 K36A.

claim: Rtt109 binds to the DNA entry-exit site near residues identified in the termination screen.
source: Although structural evidence shows that the acetyltransferase for H3 K56, Rtt109, binds to the DNA entry-exit site near residues identified here (Zhang et al., 2018), our mutants do not display global reductions in H3 K56ac, and the H3 K56A mutant was not identified as termination-defective in our screen.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: The DNA entry-exit site mutants do not display global reductions in H3 K56ac.
source: Although structural evidence shows that the acetyltransferase for H3 K56, Rtt109, binds to the DNA entry-exit site near residues identified here (Zhang et al., 2018), our mutants do not display global reductions in H3 K56ac, and the H3 K56A mutant was not identified as termination-defective in our screen.
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The H3 K56A mutant was not identified as termination-defective in the screen.
source: Although structural evidence shows that the acetyltransferase for H3 K56, Rtt109, binds to the DNA entry-exit site near residues identified here (Zhang et al., 2018), our mutants do not display global reductions in H3 K56ac, and the H3 K56A mutant was not identified as termination-defective in our screen.
evidence: This claim is stated directly in the text.

claim: H3 K42 can be methylated in S. cerevisiae.
source: Among the residues identified in our screen, H3 K42 can be methylated in S. cerevisiae and replacement of this residue with alanine has been reported to cause a 'hypertranscription phenotype' marked by increased intergenic and genic RNA levels (Hyland et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hyland et al., 2011.

claim: Replacement of H3 K42 with alanine has been reported to cause a 'hypertranscription phenotype' marked by increased intergenic and genic RNA levels.
source: Among the residues identified in our screen, H3 K42 can be methylated in S. cerevisiae and replacement of this residue with alanine has been reported to cause a 'hypertranscription phenotype' marked by increased intergenic and genic RNA levels (Hyland et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hyland et al., 2011.

claim: The accumulation of intergenic and genic transcripts in the H3 T45A and H3 R52A mutants, and likely the H3 K42A strain, is due to increased sense-strand transcription 5' and 3' to gene bodies and antisense transcription overlapping gene bodies.
source: Our strand-specific RNA-seq and 4tU-seq analyses indicate that the accumulation of intergenic and genic transcripts in the H3 T45A and H3 R52A mutants, and likely the H3 K42A strain (Hyland et al., 2011), is due to increased sense-strand transcription 5' and 3' to gene bodies and antisense transcription overlapping gene bodies.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq and 4tU-seq data.

claim: One mechanism by which the DNA entry-exit site regulates termination is through controlling nucleosome stability and imposing a barrier to Pol II progression.
source: Restoration of nucleosome occupancy and transcription termination in a DNA entry-exit site mutant by a nucleosome superbinder sequence suggests that one mechanism by which the DNA entry-exit site regulates termination is through controlling nucleosome stability and imposing a barrier to Pol II progression.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the superbinder experiment results.

claim: The broad transcriptional effects of DNA entry-exit site substitutions accrue from the combined loss of interactions with multiple regulatory factors as well as potential indirect effects.
source: However, given the additional importance of the DNA entry-exit site as a target for histone modifiers and chromatin remodelers, it is reasonable to assume that the broad transcriptional effects of DNA entry-exit site substitutions accrue from the combined loss of interactions with multiple regulatory factors as well as potential indirect effects.
evidence: This claim is speculative, as indicated by the phrase 'it is reasonable to assume'.

claim: The accumulation of extended and antisense transcripts in DNA entry-exit site mutants likely imposes a burden on RNA surveillance pathways.
source: Moreover, the accumulation of extended and antisense transcripts in these mutants likely imposes a burden on RNA surveillance pathways, raising interesting questions about how these pathways feedback on the transcriptional process.
evidence: This claim is speculative, as indicated by the word 'likely'.

claim: Nucleosomes can facilitate transcription termination by serving as a barrier to transcription.
source: Our results suggest that nucleosomes can facilitate termination by serving as a barrier to transcription and highlight the importance of the DNA entry-exit site in broadly maintaining the integrity of the transcriptome.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and is supported by the superbinder experiment results.

claim: The DNA entry-exit site is important in broadly maintaining the integrity of the transcriptome.
source: Our results suggest that nucleosomes can facilitate termination by serving as a barrier to transcription and highlight the importance of the DNA entry-exit site in broadly maintaining the integrity of the transcriptome.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and is supported by the genome-wide transcription data.

claim: The H3 R40A mutant failed to show extended products at any of the SNR genes tested by northern analysis and is likely a false positive from the screen.
source: Levels of the SNR48 readthrough product were similar in all the mutants identified in our screen with the exception of the H3 R40A mutant, which failed to show extended products at any of the SNR genes tested by northern analysis and is likely a false positive from our screen.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the northern blot data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The H3 T45A and H3 R52A mutants exhibited the highest levels of 3'-extended RNAs at the SNR47 and SNR13 genes.
source: In contrast, at the SNR47 and SNR13 genes, the H3 T45A and H3 R52A mutants exhibited the highest levels of 3'-extended RNAs.
evidence: This claim is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The H2A H113A, H2A L117A and H2A S121A mutants consistently showed the strongest termination defects among H2A mutants tested.
source: We observed varying degrees of terminator readthrough in these H2A mutant strains but consistently saw the strongest defects in the H2A H113A, H2A L117A and H2A S121A mutants.
evidence: This claim is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The amino acids altered in H2A H113A, H2A L117A and H2A S121A mutants map near the positions of the amino acids in H3 that, when mutant, cause strong readthrough phenotypes.
source: The amino acids altered in these H2A mutants map near the positions of the amino acids in H3 that, when mutant, cause strong readthrough phenotypes (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the structural data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The two H3 mutants (H3 T45A and H3 R52A) are strongly correlated with respect to their extent of readthrough at all snoRNA genes.
source: With respect to their extent of readthrough at all snoRNA genes, the two H3 mutants are strongly correlated (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: At divergently oriented genes, the 5' nascent transcript enrichment cannot be attributed to terminator readthrough from the neighboring annotated gene.
source: At divergently oriented genes, the 5' nascent transcript enrichment cannot be attributed to terminator readthrough from the neighboring annotated gene.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the orientation of divergent genes.

claim: Enrichment in 3' read density at convergently oriented genes is most easily explained as an increase in terminator readthrough from at least one gene in the pair.
source: Enrichment in 3' read density at convergently oriented genes is most easily explained as an increase in terminator readthrough from at least one gene in the pair.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the orientation of convergent genes and the 4tU-seq data.

claim: The transcription patterns at some genes appear to be normal in the DNA entry-exit site mutants.
source: While we observed widespread elevations in intergenic transcripton in the mutants (Figure 4A–B), the transcription patterns at some genes appear to be normal (for examples, see Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the 4tU-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Additional studies will be needed to elucidate the mechanistic distinctions between genes that are strongly influenced by the DNA entry-exit site substitutions and those that are relatively unaffected by them.
source: Additional studies will be needed to elucidate the mechanistic distinctions between genes that are strongly influenced by the DNA entry-exit site substitutions and those that are relatively unaffected by them.
evidence: This is a statement about future research needs.

claim: The small increase in SRATs in the H3 R52A mutant over the H3 T45A mutant is not statistically significant.
source: Despite a more severe H3 K36me3 defect in the H3 R52A mutant, the small increase in SRATs in this mutant over the H3 T45A mutant is not statistically significant.
evidence: This claim is stated directly in the text and is supported by the RNA-seq data.

claim: The severity of the termination defects of the H3 T45A and H3 R52A mutants did not correlate with the strength of their H3 K36me3 defects.
source: We noticed that the severity of the termination defects of the H3 T45A and H3 R52A mutants did not correlate with the strength of their H3 K36me3 defects (Figures 1D and 5A).
evidence: This claim is inferred from comparing the data in Figures 1D and 5A.

claim: The inviability of the H3 K36A, R52A double mutant was not due to lack of expression of the double mutant histone.
source: We confirmed that the inviability was not due to lack of expression of the double mutant histone by transforming the H3 K36A, R52A-expressing plasmid into yeast cells with tagged endogenous H3 (HHT1-HA) and a deletion of the second H3-H4 locus (hht2-hhf2∆). In this context, cells retained the ability to express the double mutant H3 protein (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The phenotypes of the H3 R52A mutant are, at least in part, independent of its roles in H3 K36me3.
source: These results argue that the phenotypes of the H3 R52A mutant are, at least in part, independent of its roles in H3 K36me3.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the synthetic lethality between H3 R52A and set2∆ or H3 K36A.

claim: The transcription defects caused by DNA entry-exit site substitutions are not due to a general loss of H3 K56ac.
source: Unlike H3 K36me3, our data show that single-residue alanine substitutions in the DNA entry-exit site do not alter levels of H3 K56ac (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), suggesting that the transcription defects caused by these substitutions are not due to a general loss of this multifunctional histone modification.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Amino acid substitutions at the DNA entry-exit site are associated with loss of transcription-coupled nucleosome occupancy at specific genes.
source: Amino acid substitutions at the DNA entry-exit site are associated with loss of transcription-coupled nucleosome occupancy at specific genes, supporting a role for this nucleosomal surface in restricting access to DNA (Hainer and Martens, 2011; Hyland et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hainer and Martens, 2011 and Hyland et al., 2011.

claim: A region of reduced nucleosome occupancy over the CPS in the H3 R52A mutant correlates with a region of reduced Pol II occupancy.
source: A region of reduced nucleosome occupancy over the CPS in the mutant correlates with a region of reduced Pol II occupancy (Figure 6A,B,D,E), suggesting that the H3 R52A substitution disrupts nucleosomes which may normally slow Pol II transit in the termination region.
evidence: This claim is supported by MNase-seq and ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6A,B,D,E.

claim: Analysis of spike-in normalized read counts across the yeast genome revealed several cases of aneuploidy in the replicate H3 R52A MNase-seq datasets.
source: Indeed, analysis of spike-in normalized read counts across the yeast genome revealed several cases of aneuploidy in the replicate H3 R52A MNase-seq datasets, and presence of these aneuploid chromosomes in the analysis led to only modest agreement between the replicates (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the biplot analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–C.

claim: Computational removal of chromosomes that showed evidence of aneuploidy in the MNase-seq datasets greatly improved the correlation between replicates.
source: Computational removal of chromosomes that showed evidence of aneuploidy in our MNase-seq datasets greatly improved the correlation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the biplot analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Results from the re-analyzed datasets (with aneuploid chromosomes removed) agree with results derived from the original datasets.
source: Results from the re-analyzed datasets agree with results derived from the original datasets and further support the conclusion that the H3 R52A substitution reduces nucleosome occupancy, alters nucleosome positioning, and leads to increased sense-strand intergenic transcription 5' and 3' to gene bodies (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the re-analyzed data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The reduction in nucleosome occupancy over the CPS may contribute to transcriptional readthrough of genes.
source: This increase in RNA signal suggests that the reduction in nucleosome occupancy over the CPS may contribute to transcriptional readthrough of these genes.
evidence: This claim is speculative, as indicated by the word 'may', and is inferred from the data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The DNA entry-exit site mutants confer the Suppressor of Ty (Spt-) phenotype.
source: In accordance with widespread alterations in nucleosome occupancy and positioning, the H3 R52A mutant and other DNA entry-exit site mutants identified by our genetic screen confer phenotypes indicative of disrupted chromatin structure (Figure 6—figure supplement 2). These phenotypes include (i) the Suppressor of Ty (Spt-) phenotype (Winston, 1992), which reports on the ability to bypass the transcriptional effects of transposon insertion mutations in the promoters or 5' ends of genes
evidence: This claim is supported by the growth assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The DNA entry-exit site mutants confer the Bypass Upstream Activation Sequence (UAS) Requirement (Bur-) phenotype.
source: These phenotypes include (i) the Suppressor of Ty (Spt-) phenotype (Winston, 1992), which reports on the ability to bypass the transcriptional effects of transposon insertion mutations in the promoters or 5' ends of genes; (ii) the Bypass Upstream Activation Sequence (UAS) Requirement (Bur-) phenotype (Prelich and Winston, 1993), which measures expression from the suc2∆uas(−1900 /- 390) allele, a mutant gene lacking positive regulatory signals in the promoter
evidence: This claim is supported by the growth assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The DNA entry-exit site mutants confer the cryptic transcription initiation phenotype.
source: and (iii) the cryptic transcription initiation phenotype, which can be measured using a sensitive reporter that detects aberrant initiation within the FLO8 coding region, GAL1pr:FLO8::HIS3 (Cheung et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by the growth assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The DNA entry-exit site mutants did not exhibit the SWI/SNF Independent (Sin-) phenotype.
source: However, in contrast to the Spt-, Bur- and cryptic initiation phenotypes, the DNA entry-exit site mutants did not exhibit the SWI/SNF Independent (Sin-) phenotype, which measures the ability of histone mutants to overcome the absence of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex (Hainer and Martens, 2011; Kruger et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by the growth assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The difference in nucleosome occupancy observed at the natural sequence between the H3 R52A mutant and the wild-type strain is not apparent by ChIP qPCR.
source: We note that the difference in nucleosome occupancy observed at the natural sequence between the H3 R52A mutant and the wild-type strain (Figure 7A) is not apparent by ChIP qPCR (Figure 7C), most likely due to the limited resolution of standard ChIP.
evidence: This claim is inferred from comparing the MNase-seq data in Figure 7A with the ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 7C.

claim: The superbinder insertion removed one of three mapped Reb1 binding sites downstream of SNR48.
source: While our superbinder insertion removed one of three mapped Reb1 binding sites downstream of SNR48 (Rhee and Pugh, 2011), the phenotype of the insertion was to increase, not to decrease, termination, suggesting multiple mechanisms facilitate termination at this gene.
evidence: This claim is stated directly in the text and is supported by a citation to Rhee and Pugh, 2011.

claim: The phenotype of the superbinder insertion was to increase, not to decrease, termination at SNR48.
source: While our superbinder insertion removed one of three mapped Reb1 binding sites downstream of SNR48 (Rhee and Pugh, 2011), the phenotype of the insertion was to increase, not to decrease, termination, suggesting multiple mechanisms facilitate termination at this gene.
evidence: This claim is supported by the northern blot data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Multiple mechanisms facilitate termination at the SNR48 gene.
source: While our superbinder insertion removed one of three mapped Reb1 binding sites downstream of SNR48 (Rhee and Pugh, 2011), the phenotype of the insertion was to increase, not to decrease, termination, suggesting multiple mechanisms facilitate termination at this gene.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that removing a Reb1 binding site did not decrease termination.

claim: The superbinder results support the idea that nucleosomes can facilitate transcription termination, presumably by slowing Pol II progression and providing time for termination factors to engage and dislodge the elongation complex.
source: These results may not be generalizable to all genes, particularly those in which factors other than nucleosome occupancy or stability dictate termination efficiency. However, they support the idea that nucleosomes can facilitate transcription termination, presumably by slowing Pol II progression and providing time for termination factors to engage and dislodge the elongation complex (Fong et al., 2015; Hazelbaker et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the superbinder experiment results and is supported by citations to Fong et al., 2015 and Hazelbaker et al., 2013.

claim: Nucleosomes positioned downstream of some NNS-dependent termination sites were proposed to function as roadblock terminators.
source: Although nucleosomes positioned downstream of some NNS-dependent termination sites were proposed to function as roadblock terminators, this hypothesis was not directly tested (Roy et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Roy et al., 2016.

claim: The hypothesis that nucleosomes positioned downstream of some NNS-dependent termination sites function as roadblock terminators was not directly tested prior to this study.
source: Although nucleosomes positioned downstream of some NNS-dependent termination sites were proposed to function as roadblock terminators, this hypothesis was not directly tested (Roy et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is stated directly in the text.
